topics: Deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC)
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-06-12
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), David Park (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Ethan Rivera (Solace CTO), Janelle Mark (Head of MLOps), Samir Patel (Security Lead), Olivia Gomez (Product)

[00:00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. This is Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, with me are David our SE and Priya our CSM. How's everyone doing?
[00:00:10] Ethan Rivera: Good, thanks. Excited to kick this off.
[00:00:13] Janelle Mark: Hey all. We've got about an hour, is that right?
[00:00:16] Priya Nair: Yep, roughly an hour, we'll keep to the agenda: introductions, goals & success criteria, security checklist, deployment options, and next steps.
[00:00:25] Maya Chen: Quick note - we'll share the onboarding deck and a one-pager after the call, and David will follow up to book a technical deep dive and perf benchmark window.
[00:00:33] Olivia Gomez: Sounds good.

[00:00:40] Janelle Mark: For context, Solace Health has a new feature pipeline that needs an inference layer for clinical note summarization and triage. We're sensitive to PII and patient data residency. We'll be evaluating from both a product and security standpoint. Timeline target is a pilot in 6-8 weeks.
[00:00:58] David Park: Great, that helps. Can you share a bit about expected traffic? burstiness? typical sequence lengths?
[00:01:05] Ethan Rivera: Daily QPS is low, maybe hundreds, but we have spikes during batch processing overnight. Sequence length is variable - many are short summaries (50-150 tokens) and some long transcripts 1,000+ tokens for pre-op notes.
[00:01:20] David Park: Understood. That mix matters for batching and KV cache behavior. Our dedicated pools help for predictable throughput whereas hosted API is faster to get started but has different SLAs.

[00:01:35] Samir Patel: Security upfront - we need SOC2 and ISO docs, SSO via SAML, audit logs, KMS integration (HSM optional), and data residency controls. We may need to run in a VPC or private deployment depending on legal review.
[00:01:48] Maya Chen: That's expected. We have SOC2 artifacts and ISO docs; we'll share them. SSO/SAML and RBAC are supported. For KMS, Redwood supports customer-managed keys and HSM integrations in Private installs.
[00:02:00] Priya Nair: We'll also provide an architecture doc for the private deployment flow - what lives in the customer VPC vs our control plane.

[00:02:12] Olivia Gomez: Are audit logs available for all API calls? We need retention for 12 months.
[00:02:16] David Park: Yes, audit logs are available; retention windows can be configured. For Private deployments it's entirely within your controls; for Hosted we can extend retention as an add-on.

[00:02:28] Janelle Mark: On perf, our threshold is p95 latency under 350ms for the shorter summaries. Cost target - we're aiming to keep unit cost under a defined threshold; we want to understand batching/caching/quantization tradeoffs.
[00:02:40] David Park: For short sequences, continuous batching and prefix caching can reduce cost significantly. Quantization options (int8, 4-bit) can cut GPU memory and cost but may affect quality - we'll surface model recommendations based on your eval prompts.
[00:02:56] Maya Chen: We can run an A/B style eval during the pilot to measure quality delta vs quantized weights. We'll also provide tooling for regen and rollbacks.

[00:03:10] Ethan Rivera: About deployment mode: we prefer to start with hosted to move fast, but security may push us toward dedicated or private. What are the main tradeoffs?
[00:03:18] David Park: Hosted is fastest and easiest: lower time-to-value, simple API keys, managed scaling. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput and SLAs - useful if you need consistent p95 targets. Private/VPC gives full network control and KMS/HSM integration for compliance. We can route traffic between them and do automatic fallback.

[00:03:37] Samir Patel: If we go hosted initially, how do you ensure data doesn't persist? We need no customer PII retained beyond processing, or at least strict controls.
[00:03:44] Maya Chen: We have data retention policies and opt-in/off options. For PII-sensitive workloads we often recommend Private. But we can ensure ephemeral processing and disable logging for certain endpoints - we'll document specifics in the security packet.

[00:03:58] Olivia Gomez: Who will be our day-to-day contacts for runbooks and incidents?
[00:04:02] Priya Nair: I'll be the CSM and primary ops contact. For technical escalation, David and Maya will be involved. We also have a 24x7 support add-on for enterprise.

[00:04:12] Janelle Mark: Benchmarks - can you run perf tests against our sample dataset? We'd like to see token cost and latency numbers on both hosted and dedicated.
[00:04:19] David Park: Yes, we'll set up a benchmarking window. Ideally you provision a non-prod dataset and we run controlled load tests to measure p50/p95 latency and token throughput. We'll also test with KV cache priming to see common-case gains.
[00:04:34] Ethan Rivera: About model versions, we want reproducibility. Can you pin model versions and do canary rollouts?
[00:04:39] David Park: Absolutely - version pinning, canary/A-B rollouts, and automatic fallback policies are supported. You can also do traffic splitting by route.

[00:04:50] Maya Chen: Let's talk timeline. You said 6-8 weeks for pilot - what's the internal gating?
[00:04:55] Janelle Mark: Legal/security sign-off and infra availability. If legal pushes back, it could slide. We want to do a 2-week sandbox validation then a 4-6 week pilot.
[00:05:04] Maya Chen: Ok, so immediate next action is sandbox provision and security questionnaire.

[00:05:10] (short mute)

[00:07:00] David Park: Quick technical note - for long transcripts (1k+ tokens) we recommend streamable outputs and KV caching to avoid re-evaluating prefixes. Also consider chunking long notes for quality and latency tradeoffs.
[00:07:18] Janelle Mark: We have some pre-processing that chunks notes but preserve context; we can share that pipeline.

[00:09:05] Samir Patel: On compliance, we need to know where keys are stored: customer-managed KMS or Redwood-managed? If it's Redwood-managed, what's the key rotation policy?
[00:09:12] David Park: Customer-managed KMS is available for Dedicated/Private. For Hosted we offer an option to use customer KMS through an integration; otherwise Redwood-managed keys have rotation policies documented in the security pack.

[00:09:30] Olivia Gomez: If we choose dedicated, is there a commit term or can we do a short-term reserved pool?
[00:09:35] Maya Chen: Dedicated typically has reserved capacity contracts but we can discuss a short pilot package or flexible burst options during the onboarding phase. We'll include pricing options in the packet.

[00:09:48] Ethan Rivera: For data residency - some records must stay in EU. Can you run dedicated GPUs in a specified region?
[00:09:54] David Park: Yes, region pinning for dedicated or private is supported; for hosted we have region selection for endpoints and can route traffic accordingly.

[00:10:10] Janelle Mark: Any limitations on models we can bring? We may want to try an open foundation model and a fine-tuned variant.
[00:10:16] David Park: We support a catalog of curated open models and also can host fine-tuned customer models, subject to model compatibility and resource requirements. We'll walk through model onboarding steps in the technical deep dive.

[00:10:30] Maya Chen: We'll also provide an eval harness to run quality checks and regression alerts - important as you iterate on prompts and models.

[00:11:00] Olivia Gomez: Can you show an example of the dashboard and per-route cost breakdown?
[00:11:05] Priya Nair: We'll include screenshots in the deck; the console shows token-level cost, latency breakdowns, per-model transactions, and tracing hooks for debugging.

[00:11:22] Samir Patel: About legal and procurement - who signs the SOC2 NDA and how long does procurement usually take?
[00:11:28] Maya Chen: Procurement timelines vary; smaller deals are typically 2-3 weeks, enterprise often longer. We'll share standard contract terms; legal can engage on amendments. For SOC2 we can provide the report and also liaise with your security team for any questions.

[00:11:45] Ethan Rivera: Ok, let's make sure we get a dedicated folder for docs.
[00:11:48] Maya Chen: We'll send a shared link to the onboarding folder and upload the security artifacts, onboarding deck, and example runbooks.

[00:12:05] (noise, crosstalk)

[00:13:40] David Park: Technical note - for evaluation we recommend metrics: p50/p95 latency, steady-state throughput, token cost per million, and generation quality (ROUGE or human evals). We'll also benchmark memory usage for quantized vs non-quantized models.
[00:13:55] Janelle Mark: We'll provide sample eval prompts and a small human eval panel.

[00:15:00] Olivia Gomez: Any gotchas with SSO user provisioning? We use Okta.
[00:15:04] Priya Nair: Okta/SAML is supported; we typically do SCIM provisioning for user sync. We'll send our SSO integration guide.

[00:16:10] Samir Patel: Audit logs format? Can they be exported to our SIEM?
[00:16:14] David Park: Yes, logs can be streamed to your SIEM or exported. We'll include sample schema.

[00:18:00] Ethan Rivera: On support SLAs, what are the guaranteed response times?
[00:18:04] Maya Chen: Our enterprise SLA options include 1-hour P1 response and 24x7 escalation; standard support has business-hours responses. We'll outline tiers in the packet.

[00:20:20] Janelle Mark: For the pilot dataset, we need to scrub PHI before we hand it over. Any recommendations?
[00:20:25] David Park: We have a recommended scrub pipeline and can do a joint runbook for data handling. If you prefer, we can run on masked synthetic data first.

[00:22:00] (brief pause)

[00:24:10] Maya Chen: Recap - primary asks: security docs, sandbox provisioning, tech deep dive & benchmark, pricing options for hosted/dedicated, pilot success criteria. Any additions?
[00:24:20] Ethan Rivera: That's good. Add: confirm region pinning for EU records.
[00:24:25] Maya Chen: Noted.

[00:24:40] Priya Nair: I'll send calendar invites for the follow-ups after this call.

[00:25:00] (some background typing)

[00:30:00] David Park: One last technical point - when we run benchmarks we'll capture both cold-start latency and steady-state. Cold start includes model load time and kv cache priming; steady-state shows batching benefits.
[00:30:12] Janelle Mark: Good. We'll ensure the test harness reflects real traffic patterns.

[00:40:00] Maya Chen: Final check - who owns which action items?
[00:40:04] Priya Nair: I'll own sandbox provisioning and the onboarding folder. Maya will send the deck and pricing. David will schedule the technical deep dive. Samir will lead security questionnaire completion. Ethan will provide traffic profile and dataset.

[00:41:10] Samir Patel: We'll try to get the security doc answers back within a week.

[00:45:00] Olivia Gomez: Thanks everyone. Excited to get started.

[00:45:10] Maya Chen: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the packet and calendar invites.

[00:51:30] Call ended

Notes: transcript contains occasional transcription errors (proper nouns and acronyms). References: onboarding deck link (shared post-call), security artifacts (SOC2/ISO), SSO integration guide, benchmarking spreadsheet (to be shared).
